nodes.name: Esau
nodes.note: Genesis 36 names Esau's wives without restating his father; 1 Chronicles 1:34 names Isaac. Shown together.

nodes.name: Anah
nodes.note: Genesis 36:20 lists Anah among the sons of Seir, but 36:24 calls Zibeon his father. Both readings are shown; they are not merged.

nodes.name: Jacob
nodes.note: Called Israel in 1 Chronicles 1:34 and 2:1-2: Israel is the name God gave Jacob (Genesis 32:28).

nodes.name: Ozias
nodes.note: Matthew 1:8 telescopes the line: Ahaziah, Joash and Amaziah stand between Jehoram and Uzziah (see 1 Chronicles 3:11-12).

nodes.name: Jechonias
nodes.note: Matthew 1:11 telescopes the line: Jehoiakim stands between Josiah and Jeconiah (see 1 Chronicles 3:15-16).

nodes.name: Zorobabel
nodes.note: Ezra, Nehemiah and Haggai name Shealtiel as father; 1 Chronicles 3:19 names Pedaiah. Both are shown.

nodes.name: Jesus
nodes.note: Matthew names Mary as mother (Matthew 1:16); Luke names Joseph as father "as was supposed" (Luke 3:23). Both lines are shown.

nodes.name: Sala
nodes.note: Luke 3:35-36 names Sala son of Cainan son of Arphaxad, while Genesis 11:12 names Shelah son of Arphaxad directly. The extra Cainan in Luke's list is a known crux; both readings are shown, not harmonized.

nodes.name: Cainan
nodes.note: This Cainan appears only in Luke 3:36, between Sala and Arphaxad; Genesis 11 has no Cainan here. Shown as stated, not harmonized.

nodes.name: Uz
nodes.note: 1 Chronicles 1:17 lists this name among the sons of Shem, while Genesis 10 names a different father. Both traditions are shown.

nodes.name: Hul

nodes.name: Meshech

nodes.name: Gazez
nodes.note: Gazez appears as a son of Ephah and as a son of Haran (1 Chronicles 2:46). Both are shown; they may be the same person.

nodes.name: Zerubbabel
nodes.note: Ezra, Nehemiah and Haggai name Shealtiel as father; 1 Chronicles 3:19 names Pedaiah. Both are shown.

nodes.name: Elkanah
nodes.note: Elkanah son of Jeroham is named in two Chronicles lines (6:26-27, where Jeroham's father is Eliab, and 6:33-38, where it is Eliel); both entries share this node, and both fathers are shown.

nodes.name: Azariah
nodes.context: son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum (1 Chronicles 6:13)
nodes.note: A second Azariah son of Hilkiah appears in 1 Chronicles 9:11, son of a different Hilkiah (son of Meshullam). Both are shown; they are not merged.

nodes.name: Adam
nodes.note: Adam had no human parents: God formed him from the dust of the ground (Genesis 2:7), and Luke 3:38 calls him "the son of God".

nodes.name: Elkanah
nodes.note: 1 Chronicles 6:26 introduces this Elkanah afresh ('As for Elkanah'), distinct from Elkanah son of Jeroham lower in the same chain; his own father is not stated.

nodes.name: Abiah
nodes.note: Shown as a distinct person: resolving this parent to any same-named profile would link to someone of the wrong sex; their own father is not stated in the passage.
